title: Determine Color of a Chessboard Square
statement:
A standard chessboard has 8 columns labelled `a` to `h` from left to right and 8 rows labelled `1` to `8` from bottom to top. The bottom-left square `a1` is black, and any two squares that share a side have different colours.

`coordinates` is a two-character string naming one square: its column letter followed by its row digit. Return `true` if that square is white and `false` if it is black. The string always names a real square of the board.
notes:
## Intuition

Colours alternate along every row and every column, so moving one square in any straight direction flips the colour. Number the columns `a` to `h` as 1 to 8. Every step changes `column + row` by exactly 1, which flips its parity, just as it flips the colour. Since `a1` has sum 2 (even) and is black, every even sum is black and every odd sum is white. Painting the whole board and looking the square up also works, but the parity rule needs no board at all.

## Approach

1. Split `coordinates` into its `letter` and its `digit`.
2. Turn `letter` into `column` from 1 to 8 by subtracting the code of `'a'` and adding 1.
3. Turn `digit` into `row` from 1 to 8 by subtracting the code of `'0'`.
4. Add them into `sum`.
5. Return `true` exactly when `sum` is odd.

## Example 1, step by step

For `"a1"`: `column = 1`, `row = 1`, `sum = 2`. Two is even, so the square is black and the answer is `false`. For comparison, `"h3"` gives `8 + 3 = 11`, which is odd, so it is white.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): two character codes and one addition.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Get the anchor right: `a1` is black, so odd sums are white, not even ones.
- `digit` is a character; adding it to a number in JavaScript concatenates strings. Convert it first.
- Starting columns at 0 instead of 1 is fine only if rows also start at 0; mixing the two flips every answer.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `letter`, `digit` | the two characters of `coordinates` |
| `column` | column number, 1 for `a` up to 8 for `h` |
| `row` | row number from 1 to 8 |
| `sum` | `column + row`; its parity decides the colour |

narration.2: The first character is the column letter.
narration.3: The second character is the row digit.
narration.4: Turn the column letter into a number from 1 (a) to 8 (h).
narration.5: Turn the row digit into a number from 1 to 8.
narration.6: One step in any direction changes this sum by one, just as it flips the colour.
narration.7: a1 has an even sum and is black, so an odd sum means white.
